name: Traditional Hydraulic Lime Mortar (Chuna-Kankar / Class A-B Lime)
traditional_use: Bedding mortar, submerged foundation masonry joints, and water-retaining revetments across Baolis and Vavs.

moisture_behavior.drying_rate: Rapid evaporation allows trapped moisture to escape without building hydraulic pore pressure
moisture_behavior.summary: Maintains continuous hygric equilibrium with surrounding masonry, allowing subsurface moisture to breathe out naturally.

mechanical_characteristics.stiffness: Low to moderate modulus of elasticity
mechanical_characteristics.ductility: High deformability, accommodates foundation settlement and seasonal micro-movement without fracturing
mechanical_characteristics.sacrificial_behavior: True sacrificial behavior: softer and more flexible than adjacent historic stone blocks
mechanical_characteristics.summary: Acts as an elastic cushion that absorbs shear and ground settlement stresses, preserving the stone units.

thermal_characteristics.thermal_shock_resilience: High tolerance to diurnal thermal cycles
thermal_characteristics.compatibility_with_historic_stones: Thermal expansion coefficient (6-8 x 10^-6 /K) closely matches sandstone and quartzite (7-11 x 10^-6 /K)
thermal_characteristics.summary: Prevents interfacial shearing stress between mortar and stone during extreme semi-arid temperature swings.

chemical_considerations.ph_nature: Alkaline (pH 11.5 - 12.5), protecting embedded metal cramps from galvanic oxidation
chemical_considerations.soluble_salts_risk: Zero introduced soluble sulfates or sodium/potassium alkalis
chemical_considerations.reactivity_with_limestone: Fully compatible chemically; undergoes autogenous healing via carbonation (Ca(OH)2 + CO2 -> CaCO3)
chemical_considerations.summary: Chemically harmonious with historic stone minerals; autogenous healing seals microcracks naturally over decades.

reversibility.extraction_method: Soft mechanical chisel, rake, or pneumatic micro-chisel without damaging host stone edges
reversibility.retreatability: Fully retreatable; leaves no insoluble synthetic residue in stone pore structure

heritage_compatibility.iks_alignment: Direct continuation of traditional Indian kankar-chuna and hydraulic slaking methods
heritage_compatibility.asi_intach_compliance: Conforms fully to ASI Architectural Conservation Manual (2020) and INTACH Charter (2004)

limitations: Historic mortar composition varies regionally based on kankar nodule calcination and slaking age.
Laboratory petrographic and XRD characterization is mandatory before formulating exact replication mixes.
